correctness.rationale: For r=(b₂−2)/(b₂−b₁), the affine derivative identity r f₁′+(1−r)f₂′=2 proves balance and admissibility, with 0<S<2. From the two branch CDFs the difference of the candidate primitives satisfies H(u)=H(f₂⁻¹f₁(u)). Because f₂>f₁ strictly inside the half interval, the iterate tends to zero, where H vanishes. Absolute continuity thus forces p(u)+p(u+1/2)=S(u) almost everywhere. Each map-specific pushforward of the uniform input has constant density r or 1−r. Conditional on any previous label history the next input remains uniform by induction with fresh choices, which is the required iid assertion. Conditioning on the original half gives covariance C₀−(1/2)∫hΔ; Δ>0 inside, so the pointwise extremizers are feasible and interpolation attains every intermediate value. Exact independent integration gives C₀=131/1920, ∫h₊Δ=55/512 and ∫h₋Δ=9/512, hence endpoints 223/15360 and 913/15360, width 23/512 and symmetric value 71/1920. No uniqueness of other invariant laws or coordinate independence is needed. In the proof, the displayed transfer density is understood almost everywhere or as a choice of version, consistently with measurable controls.
residual_risks: The numerical values checked exactly are for the specified canonical pair only; the general classification, iid law and optimality come from the proof, not sampling.

value.rationale: This is a sharp answer to an identifiable inverse question on the published map pair: even identical uniform marginals and identical entire iid switching laws leave a positive, exactly quantified freedom in a basic two-time statistic. The complete extremal and attainability statements are more informative than a single computed covariance or a demonstration of nonuniqueness.
residual_risks: The scope is coordinate lag one for this pair; it is not a characterization of all time correlations or a general optimization theorem for unrelated maps.
